items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: For many years I recorded Roberto Carlos, who is from Brazil.

ctx.x: Was it partly the lyric content that led you in the direction?
I can’t really say that it was any one thing. For many years I recorded Roberto Carlos, who is from Brazil. And I understand Portuguese and he would play me his demo on a © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

piano, or on a keyboard, that he had recorded. And I heard him singing in Portuguese but he would tell me what it meant in English. And as he would tell me the story I could get the feeling of what he was saying. And the interesting part about – I learned about making records is when you listen to a record you may not remember what the lyric says. You may not remember what the melody was all at one time. But you’ll really remember how it made you feel. So the whole idea was to get you to feel exactly what I felt…
